Patch Notes

Made general improvements to performance and frame rate.
Improved memory usage during shader precompile.
Added save state backups.
Fixed bug causing some achievements to not be shown or awarded, including Humankind and Perfect Memory.
Adjusted font sizes on Steam Deck.
Hardcoded quality and stability settings on Steam Deck.
We're still working on getting After Us Steam Deck verified. Please stay tuned for any updates! If you're encountering an issue that is not listed above, please contact our support team directly for help.

notes.title: After Us is Available Now!
notes.content:
The time has come to revive the souls of extinct animals. After Us is out now.

We have put a lot of love into this game and we want to thank all the people that have shared their efforts, hopes, and wishes with us to make this happen. We would like After Us to resonate with players all around the world and instill a bit of hope in their hearts.

Thank you so much for the support! We hope you connect with Gaia and her journey as we have.

So much passion went into this game. An important part of the experience in After Us is the amazing soundtrack composed by Dan Elms. Haunting, melancholic, dream-like, spooky, delicate...it's a very personal combination of layered sounds, epic passages, and evocative melodies that will take you by the hand and set the mood as you explore the world. We are so proud of it and as a thank you, we wanted to give a little extra to everyone that supports us here at Piccolo. When you purchase the game here on Steam, you will also receive the soundtrack included with your purchase! We hope everyone enjoys it as much as we do!

Please enjoy our launch trailer that encapsulates the desolation yet hope in this game. If you want to learn more about the game from co-game directors Alexis Corominas and Jordi Ministral, check out our Q&A where they answered some of your questions!

From the Piccolo family, thank you for playing! ❤

notes.title: Q&A with Piccolo Studio
notes.content:
After Us launches in less than a week on May 23rd!

Ahead of release over at Piccolo Studio, we wanted to take a moment and answer some questions we gathered from the community about our game. We can't wait for you to experience this surrealistic exploration adventure game, so let's find out a bit more from Alexis Corominas and Jordi Ministral, Co-Game Directors.

Do you have any tips for players in After Us?

Alexis: Soak in the world. Don't look at it like the type of game where you have to upgrade your skill tree or improve your character's abilities, because we don't do that. After Us is a game about exploring and thinking about what you're seeing - being moved by the environment, the main character, and the experiences you're going to have.
What inspired you to tell the story of After Us? How does it compare to your studio's first title, Arise: A Simple Story?

Alexis: Well, Arise: A Simple Story was the tale of an old man looking back. For After Us, we wanted to change that and wanted to look ahead. Look ahead on what legacy we are leaving for our children, and even beyond that - for future generations. It explores what kind of relationship we have with the environment and this planet.
What can you tell us about the protagonist, Gaia, and her abilities?

Alexis: Gaia is a small nymph who lives in the Ark. This is a game about desolation and hope. She is the light of the game, she is hope. We wanted to have a very quick character, so she can run very fast while exploring the world. She also jumps very high, double-jumps, can dodge in the air, and as we see later on, she can use her heart for special abilities.
Based on what we've seen so far, the world of After Us seems tragic, yet beautiful. Was that your intention? Additionally, what were your inspirations while building the world?

Alexis: We wanted to create a very unique world that shows how humans interact with nature. It's the world after us - the world after humans have destroyed everything, a world devoid of any life full of concrete and steel. It has a layer of melancholy but we wanted to make it beautiful. We spent a lot of time creating the world and the right balance between a bleak world and a visually compelling world.
What was the art process like designing the environments, Gaia, and the spirits?

Jordi: We start with high-level concepts like: deciding this section of the world is about this concept, and figure out how to represent that visually. I don't know about other companies, but I think maybe this is where we are slightly different. We don't have design teams working on one part at a time. We have the animators, the environment artists, and the designers work at the same time, together. When designers are thinking about a puzzle, they need to have a sense of the layout and the artistic vision. We don't want the puzzle to feel like a puzzle out of context.
Gaia not only can restore animal spirits, but she possesses the ability to regrow plant life. Can you tell us more about what this does and how it impacts gameplay?

Alexis: The player has an ability called "Burst of Life", the ability to grow vegetation around Gaia. It can be used to deal with hazards, like in combat or removing patches of oil so you can freely pass. There are even certain elements in the world that you can grow that will stay forever. We want the player to feel like they are impacting the world. Not just by creating trees here and there, but also because you are restoring spirits to the world.
What are the achievements going to be? Any difficulty or speedrun ones or just a straightforward list?

Jordi: The achievements are more of a straightforward list, like getting an achievement for collecting all the animals in an area, or for growing a certain amount of trees. Achievements are probably one of the more conventional rewards we give to players in After Us.
It seems fans have really resonated seeing the dog spirit from the game. Can you tell us more about how you picked which animals to include and do you have any stories about what inspired those?

Alexis: The weiner dog is the first animal vessel you find in After Us. We wanted a small, domestic dog because it resonates a lot more. It's a vulnerable animal and has a collar, so you know it was someone's animal. For us, it's like the last dog, and this corpse represents all the dogs.
Jordi: You will see that we have the deer and the shark that represent big families of animals.
Alexis: The shark is interesting because everybody would expect to be moved by the dog. But managing to move people by the shark? I think that was a bigger challenge. You are seeing the world through the eyes of Gaia, and she doesn't have this human perception of animals. The dog and the shark are just the same: life-beings.
Without spoiling anything, which part of After Us do you think players will enjoy the most?

Alexis: The game has a lot of biomes, and sometimes gameplay changes depending on them. So, players may enjoy a specific area of the game. I think that people who really get into the loop of exploring the world and finding all the hidden spirits, as well as people that enjoy the emotional side of the game, are really going to enjoy After Us.
What message do you hope players will take away from the game?

Jordi: I hope when people finish the game they take away this message of hope: in the end, the only way to make the world a better place is to try.
Alexis: It's not a message we want people to take away from this game, but a feeling.

notes.title: After Us Previews and Gameplay Trailer
notes.content:
Hey After Us fans!

The previews for After Us have just been released, and we are so excited about the response! Early impressions about the game are incredibly positive, we are delighted to read that people find beauty and hope in desolation. Players are empathizing with Gaia, alone in a bleak world. It was so important for us that players make Gaia's feelings their own as well. Many previews highlight how the game makes you feel and think about humans and nature. We don't want to judge, we just want to move people and stimulate conversations, so mission accomplished!

But don’t just take out the word for it, check out the previews for yourself! And make sure to pick up After Us when released on May 23rd.  


“After Us is a beautiful abstract exploration game with a powerful message.” – GameInformer

“With the addition of gorgeous graphics and stellar animation, After Us skillfully crafts and spreads the message of achievable hope and optimism for the state of the world.” - NoisyPixel

“If After Us wasn't on your radar before, it should be now!” – GamesRadar+
